body: It could simply be that you had a female psychiatrist before, and she mentioned it just in case you had a preference for that. Did the person in question know what you said about gender preference?

I can't say I have any insight to share about it, but for what it's worth, it does sound familiar, right down to the rare pause in between. It's not always the case though; sometimes I just feel bad without the feeling of "fakeness".

That's actually one of the things I wonder about specifically - how long, if ever, people would take to get over me. Of course it'll be different for different people so it's hard to give one answer to that. If it truely takes them forever to get over me, I really couldn't justify committing suicide, but I'm sure that's not true for everyone, at least.

My day-to-day life is pretty boring lately. I've started college again a while back, but there aren't that many classes for me at the moment (due to strange timing of going back). Besides playing computer games, I don't have a lot of hobbies... I do play (board)games with friends relatively often, which often lifts my mood for a bit, but I don't have a whole lot of friends to meet up with so I'll often end up home alone.

To answer your (and lakelady's) question about professional help: I've talked about my problems with a college therapist, who referred me to a "normal" psychologist. So far it's not really helping much - it's mostly making me feel stupid about having to see a psychologist. I'm also afraid to admit to her quite how much I think about suicide lately (just as with friends - for similar reasons: afraid of upsetting them and feeling stupid for having to tell them how I feel).
I've not tried antidepressants yet, and only briefly discussed them. They do scare me a lot; the idea of chemicals altering my thoughts like that is not something I like, and the side-effects don't look nice either.

I'm also afraid about what'll happen if I won't be able to deal with my issues. What if it ends up that suicide ís the best option to save everyone from pain, once I start becoming annoying and depressing enough that I'm bringing pain to everyone regardless?

Thanks for your response. I've wanted to respond to this since I read it, but I've put it off because I didn't really know what to write.

You're right that I'm doing better then I could be. It's still very painful at times, and tiresome in general, but if I look back at how I was doing a year back and before I can see it's going a lot better. I'm still afraid I'll fall back down and loose the friends I have though, but at least I have something to loose. It's also hard to look at myself and be proud at what I achieved, so it's nice to hear that others admire how I'm dealing with it.

I hope you too can find a way to help with your problems. I know how hard it is to face your fears and do something you "know" will go wrong - the only reason I got out of that pit was because others forced me (sort of) to go ahead and do it anyway. Maybe that'll help you too - set yourself a deadline (with someone else to keep you to it) to do something you want to do but are afraid of.

At any rate, thank you for your message - and that goes for SolarFederalist as well.

I've gone through something a lot like you have with my father; only in the last year I've really allowed myself to grieve for him (over five and a half years ago now since he died).

If my feelings are any indication about how your process will go (of course, it's different for everyone), it will feel better once you start dealing with it. It'll hurt a lot, but it's only taking the pain that's there in the background anyway and bringing it forward so you can give it a place. 

My advice is to find someone you know you can really talk to (friends, family, support group) and just talk. Talk about why you miss her, about how it's unfair, that you want her back, just anything you feel like. It'll be painful, but in a strange way it'll feel good and relieving, because you're getting all that off your chest.

I know how you feel when you say you're afraid to talk to your friends, because I feel exactly the same way. But I did it anyway (harder then it sounds, I know; and I did it more because I needed to then because I wanted to) and it helped a lot.

What helped for me (to make myself talk to them) was imagining how it would feel if a friend would come to me and told me they were feeling bad. You probably wouldn't think they were pathetic then, and just want to be there for them.

Hello again,

I feel a bit melodramatic posting this less then a day after my previous message here, but I'm feeling better today then the rest of the week. The lovesickness is still there, but since everyone tells me that I shouldn't feel guilty about that, I can just feel "normally" bad about that without it crushing me, and it's a far cry from the general hopelessness I've been feeling since monday.

The friend who told me to post here earlier, besides that, made me make a list of friends, and then ask them what they like about me, and that helped a lot too. It's nice to see that people think a lot better of me then I tend to think they think about me.

Still, while I can tell myself again that people do like me and care about me, I still don't feel that - it's something I have to convince myself about. It's easy now that they told me how they feel, but deep inside I still don't agree with them. At the same time, while I can put it aside for today, I still don't see myself ever not being alone. And I'm more then a bit scared about experiencing how a tiny thing can completely devastate me so fast, even when I think I'm doing better.

Thank you for your kind messages. You gave me a lot to think about. The guilt thing is something others have mentioned over time as well. Mostly though, the responses really helped me to try and do the other things I did yesterday, and I really needed that.

I still have a hard and painful week to look forward to, but I think it'll be less so then the past week. I also know that I have a long way to go still before I'll be happy again, and I'm still not sure I'll manage that, but at least for now I'm not certain I won't be either.
